brief: A PLA dome: exactly half of a 70 mm sphere, sitting flat side to the left side, hollow on the inside. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

requirements.statement: The dome shall be 35 mm along X.
The dome's extent in Y equals the 70 mm sphere diameter, as the hemisphere is round about the axis perpendicular to its flat face.
The dome shall be 70 mm along Z.
The dome is round about the axis through its flat face (its curved surface is a true hemispherical section).
The dome is exactly half of a 70 mm diameter sphere.
The dome's shell shall be 2 mm thick (assumed: the brief gives no wall).
The dome's flat face shall be turned to the left: a rim 2 mm wide, at least 214 mm^2 of it lying flat there.
The flat side shall be open, 33 mm deep at the middle: half of a hollow sphere.

assumptions.statement: The hollow shell has a wall thickness of 2 mm, a conventional value for a PLA FDM printed hollow decorative shell of this size.
assumptions.rationale: The brief specifies the part is hollow but gives no wall thickness; 2 mm is a typical minimum printable and reasonably robust wall for PLA at this scale.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: A thinner wall may be fragile or fail to print cleanly; a thicker wall increases mass and reduces internal cavity volume beyond what the user may want.

assumptions.statement: The flat circular face of the hemisphere is open (not capped), since the brief describes it as hollow and mentions no base or cap closing it.
assumptions.rationale: A dome with no mention of a closing base, sitting flat side down/left, is conventionally an open shell like a bowl or cover.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: If the flat face should be closed, the part would need an added base disc, changing its mass and print requirements.

assumptions.statement: The part is manufactured in PLA via FDM 3D printing, as stated in the brief; no specific PLA grade or print settings are assumed beyond this.
assumptions.rationale: The brief names PLA directly as the material.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: Not applicable; this is stated, not assumed, other than the fabrication method implied by material choice.

assumptions.statement: The part's flat cut face is modeled facing the -X direction ('left'), with the dome's curved surface extending in +X, and the hemisphere's axis of symmetry lying along X.
assumptions.rationale: The brief states the flat side sits to the left; this fixes an orientation convention for the geometry.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: If 'left' refers to a different global axis convention, the part's orientation in the model would not match the intended real-world placement, though the shape itself is unaffected.

unknowns.question: What wall thickness should the hollow dome shell have?
unknowns.why_it_matters: Wall thickness drives the part's mass, printability, and structural robustness even though it carries no load; an assumed default may not match the user's intended look or weight.

unknowns.question: Should the flat circular face of the hemisphere be open (like a bowl/cover) or closed with a flat base/cap?
unknowns.why_it_matters: This determines whether the part is a true open shell or a closed hollow hemisphere, materially changing its geometry and mass.

notes: REQ_BOUNDING_BOX_Z carried `source: "user"` against a threshold the brief does not state. The figure may be sound -- a derived dimension, a manufacturing limit -- but the user did not write it, so it is recorded as `derived` rather than reported back to them as their own requirement.
dropped 1 load question(s): the brief states that this part carries no load, so there was nothing to be uncertain about
REQ_BOUNDING_BOX_X claimed the part 70 mm along X, the whole sphere's diameter; the brief's 70 mm dome is 35 mm that way, and the claim now says so.
REQ_BOUNDING_BOX_Z claimed the part 35 mm along Z, a figure the brief never wrote; the brief's 70 mm dome is 70 mm that way, and the claim now says so.
added ASM_WALL_THICKNESS at 2 mm: the brief makes the part hollow and gives no wall, and the design cannot be drawn without one. It is a guess and is recorded as one.

added REQ_WALL_THICKNESS at 2 mm, REQ_FLAT_FACE, REQ_OPEN_FLAT_SIDE at 33 mm deep: the brief makes the part half of a hollow 70 mm sphere -- a shell 2 mm thick (assumed), open on its flat side -- and a solid half sphere has the same size. Its wall is measured as the thinnest wall anywhere: a shell is that thick all the way round.

document.name: Hollow hemisphere dome
document.description: Half of a 70 mm sphere, hollow with a 2 mm wall, open on its flat face which faces left (-X). Built as a full sphere and a hollow sphere shell, each intersected with a half-space box, so the flat face passes through the sphere's centre.
